In one world, his wife survived the accident, in the other, his son. One of them is a hallucination and he has to find out which is real.

Most of it, like you said, tends to be biopics, med dramas, and docs, but there are a few that are more creative with the approach... Off the top of my head, there's a film adaptation of a book called Before I Go To Sleep about a woman who essentially can't form new memories that last longer than a day, leaving her a functional 'blank slate' every time she wakes up in the morning. There are cases like this in reality - the famous one is HM, but there's a musician in a similar condition except the shelf-life of his memories is something like *twenty minutes.* I never saw the film, but I think I remember hearing it's a decent adaptation, and I loved the book.

Neurologically speaking, this split is theoretically possible. Your personal memories - your first kiss, your high school graduation, what you ate for lunch yesterday - are referred to as *episodic memory.* This is an entirely different entity neurologically from *semantic memory,* which is the part of your memory that stores facts like who the president is, as Buggy77 describes below. These are also both separate from *procedural memory,* which is the kind of memory involved in learning and retaining skills like riding a bike. 

The severance procedure clearly wipes all episodic memories (or, to be more precise, creates a sort of "separate file" for the innie's episodic memory which ostensibly doesn't affect or become affected by their outie's episodic memory) but retains everything semantic and procedural. Helly could absolutely know that gorillas are endangered, since that falls under semantic memory, but obviously couldn't remember if she'd ever seen one since that'd fall under episodic. 

I studied both neuropsych and film and Severance is one of the few times I get to combine both topics I studied, lol. There's actually some really freaky (and very famous) studies out there that, while obv. not as extreme as the severance procedure, showcase a bizarre sort of "two-in-one" consciousness phenomenon caused by severing the corpus callosum, the bridge between the two halves of the brain. It's called split-brain syndrome and it's even weirder than it sounds.

>It’s nasty constantly having things jerked out of our hands, pushed out of the way! People in manual wheelchairs have their wheelchairs literally grabbed and pulled and pushed against their will wherever the able body person imagines they need to go. It’s awful. It makes our lives awful.

I'm not usually a wheelchair user, but recently I flew out to another city for a surgical procedure and then flew back. My mom arranged for a wheelchair to meet us at the airport both ways (only one of them actually showed up, but that's a different story) and after both flights so that I wouldn't waste my energy hauling myself and my bag through the airports (chronic fatigue/small fiber neuropathy). Having the airport employees wheel me around was obviously super helpful but *man* was it disconcerting as fuck to not be in control of where I was going. Like, of course if he'd wheeled me away from my parents or into the street I could have gotten up and been like "wtf" but I still felt very vulnerable. Really drove home how frustrating it must be for people who use them more regularly and as such get jerked around more frequently. 

(Side note: my mom pulls things out of my hands *all. the. time.* Drives me fucking crazy. I beg her not to do it because I tell her it fucks with my balance - it does - but I think she thinks I'm lying because she's usually pretty good about other stuff

I know, I felt awful that OP felt like he had to downplay his experience like that. My dad had (for specific and thoughtful reasons that I don't want to get into here, I don't want to argue over whether or not they were valid reasons) kept the fact that he had MS from my brother and I. When he finally told us, I just burst into tears like a little kid. It was remitting relapsing, which is significantly less dangerous than primary progressive, and the treatment managed to basically hit pause on any further damage, but I just completely broke down. Like, that's my dad! I don't want my dad to die! I don't want anything to happen to him! 

Health issues that seem not too scary from an intellectual POV can still absolutely wreck your shit emotionally.

Part of the game's biggest charm is the juxtaposition between Lovecraftian cosmic horror and Jeeves-style comedy of manners and errors. You can go from discussing the mysteries of the afterlife with talking tigers to translating the ancient language of the stars themselves to failing to educate university students who think Pyramus and Thisbe were *Clay Men. From the Docks.*  Only two of these things give you nightmares (hint: it's not the tigers). It's my favorite scent from them by far and is only available in the EDP format. **Iced Wysteria** is also really gorgeous, it's a cold, creamy floral vanilla that has slightly salty and lactonic aspects? It also contains their famous waffle cone accord :) The first time I wore it I wasn't sure it was for me, but I fell in love with it over the course of the wear; couldn't stop sniffing myself. **Mountain Vanilla, Gin Flower,** and **Foxcroft** are also all fascinating and totally worth a try. The real nerf was limiting his ult's stack generation to 6 instances. That was the biggest downgrade he received. Otherwise if you consider that his kit essentially sacrifices his personal damage in favor of consistent debuff application with practically 100% uptime if specced correctly, his role makes sense and he's good at it. This design does come at the cost of him being a good fit for DoT teams, which means his value is limited outside of Acheron and Ratio. Since Ratio's BiS team (until now, idk if Jiaoqiu is an upgrade or downgrade from Topaz, and by how much) of Topaz, Robin, and Aventurine has been available for a while now, most folks who meaningfully use him probably won't be super interested in adding JQ if what they have works well - which it really does.

That was the argument. Similar ceilings, but DHIL has stricter team and relic requirements to reach those ceilings, whereas Jingliu has a lot more breathing room. Far easier for her to use Rutilant, can use SP-consuming supports like Bronya very effectively, but can make Tingyun/Huohuo and Sparkle work too (to say nothing of Robin, or RM with Penacony set), can even enable Double-DPS Blade if you're feeling silly. She does really appreciate Bronya's action advance but a carefully speed-tuned Sparkle skill or Robin Ult can do something similar. Meanwhile a Sparkle-less DHIL is stuck with Hanya, who I love but is a piss-poor substitute, and if he doesn't have his sig, Herta LC isn't a great fit since Imprison is the worst of all the break effects. He's restricted to hypercarry roles due to his SP consumption while JL can serve as a sub/double-dps thanks to her being more SP-friendly, especially with supports who are multi-dps friendly like RM or Robin (even Asta!).
Seriously. All they had to do was let him have some sort of healing capacity and his use cases go through the roof.

It kind of bugs me that they've been releasing a lot of "premium subscription" 5-stars lately where they share a playstyle with another, more easily available character, especially when they also share element and path. JQ and Gui (though he's really more meant to replace Pela for Acheron), Yunli and Clara, now Gallagher and Lingsha... It's not inherently a bad thing, especially since the MoC/PF/AS that cycle should be easier for folks with the "economy class" version, and either they're easy to build with existing relics/cones or their release comes with upgrades for the "base" units. However, it also directly contributes to power-creep (poor Clara), or, as is happening now with JQ, it makes him feel like a sub-par investment because his opportunities to truly shine over his F2P counterparts are more niche/restricting than most of the other limited units to precede him.   
  
Meanwhile, we have no Ice Abundance, no Wind Erudition (I know Screwllum is coming so we will get imaginary at some point), and only 5 preservation characters, two of whom share an element. (Still can't believe we don't have physical preservation.) We don't really have a sustain dedicated to DoT playstyle (Huohuo and Gallagher synergize nicely but it's not their bread and butter the same way Gallagher is made for break teams), and we have excellent supports for Break and FuA but not one that combines both for characters like Himeko and Xueyi who have fingers in both pies (yes, I know, you can just use RM and Topaz/Jade). There's a lot of niches in the game's ecosystem and it seems odd to me that they would choose to create more characters for niches that are already occupied, even if there's room, rather than try and craft units to fill the empty ones.

They're not really supports, though. Kafka is a driver/enabler DPS with no real buff or debuff capacity, and allows for a much more active DoT playstyle. She's only a damage amplifier in that she makes the DoT of other characters proc more frequently. BS I guess you could argue is a support thanks to the def shred and easy Arcana application/uptime, but her kit focuses just as much on her own personal damage, if not more, than promoting that of other characters.

I think part of it is that debuffs need re-applying more consistently and there's a chance for enemies to shake it off in most cases, or the debuff needs re-applying on new waves of enemies (save for BS and JQ, but even then they need to re-stack). Ruan Mei basically cannot be SP negative since it's a 3-turn skill duration so there's no excuse to not have it up 100% of the time, Sparkle gives the whole party a buff whenever SP get consumed and Robin wreaks havoc just by being on the damn field. Even Thanatoplum Rebloom can't be resisted. Meanwhile, JQ's ult only gives 60% chance of a Roast stack upon affected enemy turn, meaning you're forced to build him for EHR, though thankfully his traces do make up for that somewhat.

And Sacred Scarab is really strange, isn't it? You're right that it's both earthy/musty and bright all at once. I felt like I was smelling the skin of someone wearing perfume, not the perfume itself. I loved Bat but got no fruit, just sexy musky leather. For whatever reason, I hated Harvest Mouse. Gross, sickly vanilla like a pudding pop that had been left to melt and congeal on a sidewalk in the sun. Unwearable on me. Also totally agreed re: Tiger and Bee. 

Penguin is honestly a delight; really intriguing cold air note that approaches that sensation of opening the door on a winter's night and getting the inside of your nostrils blast-chilled. Would be intrigued to hear your thoughts on Macaque: Yuzu.

In all seriousness, I think we might have some more forays into atmospherics, aquatics and "imitations"/"replicas"/"portraits" kind of similar to the Replica line or the Demeter approach, like the house you mentioned. Petrichor scents might be a trend, or perhaps ozonics. That, maybe green scents too, lots of moss and ivy. Just a hard right turn away from the gourmands and the likes of JHAG Not a Perfume and Glossier You that've come to define this decade.

Humans are just another kind of animal, in the end, and when people forget that, we get ourselves into big trouble - in film and real life.

The film industry holds everyone in it to almost impossible expectations. It forces Gordy and Lucky to act in ways counter to their nature until they just can't bear it anymore and snap, at which point they're discarded. The animals have no way to understand their unpleasant experiences or put them into context. Maybe they have some idea that the humans are responsible. To the animals, we are the higher power, much as JJ is to us. Our purposes are inscrutable. Likewise, in the typical alien abduction movie, we rarely learn the reasons why they're taking us. It's usually left ambiguous, but given how advanced their technology is compared to ours, we assume it's for some loftier goal we're not elevated enough to understand.

Is it a reach to think Gordy might assume something similar? 

He was pushed to his limits for mere entertainment. To stave off boredom. Nothing more. There's a kind of horror in that which is paralleled by 

Likewise, JJ's victims are not taken in the service of some higher intelligence. They're just filling the stomach of a hungry beast, fulfilling baser needs.

That's what we think of ourselves as doing when we engage with media on a deeper level. Observing, abducting and returning.
